scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Mountain God's Dance
This is Hayachine Kagura. 14th-15th century.
on_screen: Title card: Hayachine Kagura · Japan · 14th-15th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The tradition dates to the 14th or 15th century, with historical influences attributed to the yamabushi, or mountain-dwelling Buddhist ascetics.
Scholars have explored potential links between the development of the Kagura and the history of Noh theater.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The performance is held annually on August 1st at the Hayachine Shrine in Hanamaki to honor Seoritsu, the tutelary deity of Mount Hayachine.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance consists of twelve masked dances.
The first six are ritualistic, followed by five historical or deity-focused dances, and a final dance featuring a shishi performer.
The full cycle lasts approximately five hours.
Watch for Shishi dance.
